Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifying items before you finalize the matrix:

1) Upstream changes: when an upstream model author changes license terms (or re-licenses), how do you detect and notify downstream customers who have pinned or are using a hosted variant? What is the notification window and what artifacts do you provide to prove the change occurred?

2) Provenance manifest: can the manifest be cryptographically signed by Redwood and include upstream attestations from third-party maintainers? If so, what signing algorithm and verification steps do you support?

3) Rollforward vs rollback: for hosted deployments, what is your default behavior when a new model variant is pushed that contains critical behavior changes (e.g., hallucination regression) discovered post-deploy?

We also attached a short PDF with a couple of small follow-ups (Novus_clarifying_questions.pdf). We appreciate a concrete, bulletized reply we can include in our procurement worksheet.

Hi Alice — answering each of your clarifying points below; Lauren helped draft the provenance specifics. Short bullets you can paste into your worksheet: 

1) Upstream license changes and notification:
- Detection: we continuously scan upstream model sources and our model ingestion pipeline captures license text at ingest time. We persist both the delta and the historical license blob in our catalog.
- Notification window: for non-security or license-clarity changes we notify affected customers via email and console 30 days prior to any automatic change in hosted routing. For license revocations or re-licensing that would impact usage rights, we notify immediately and surface required action items.
- Artifacts provided: timestamped license blobs, diffs, and a signed change record (see provenance manifest).

2) Provenance manifest and signatures:
- Manifest contents: model_name, model_checksum (SHA-256), source_url, source_commit/tag, license_text_snippet, ingest_timestamp, supplier_attestations (free-text field), and redwood_signatures.
- Signing: Redwood signs manifests using ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256; signatures are attached as base64 and we publish our public key via our KMS-backed key registry. We also support optional upstream signatures if the model upstream provides them; these are included verbatim in the supplier_attestations field.
- Verification: customers can verify the SHA-256 checksum and the Redwood ECDSA signature using our published public key. We will provide a sample verification script in the Drive link below.

3) Rollforward / rollback behavior for hosted deployments: 
- Default: we do controlled rollouts. New variants are routed to a configurable percentage of traffic (canary) for a default 48-hour window. During that window we run automated regressions tied to customer-provided eval prompts (if supplied) and our internal quality checks.
- On regression: automatic rollback to the previous pinned variant if metrics exceed configured thresholds; immediate manual rollback support for customers who request it.
- For critical safety/security regressions discovered post-deploy, Redwood will: 1) throttle new sessions to the impacted region, 2) execute emergency rollback if rollback criteria are met, and 3) issue an incident report and customer notification within 4 hours.

Extras and next steps:
- We uploaded a sample provenance manifest and a verification script here: https://drive.google.com/redwood/sample-provenance-manifest
- We can provide cryptographic proof-of-immutability via signed checksums on request for Dedicated/Private customers.
- If useful, let's schedule the 30-minute technical call — propose 2026-12-08 at 10:00 AM ET. Lauren will join to show the manifest examples and redwood_response_matrix.xlsx has the full mapping.

Thanks — happy to make any edits to the bullets so they slot into your procurement worksheet cleanly.
